name: AppLogin
description: Database storage for spring security's remember-me feature

name: AppUser
description: Application users. Used to authenticate users by spring security. Can have additional fields/relations (See UserInfoService)

fieldDocs.name: created
fieldDocs.description: Creation date of the user entry

fieldDocs.name: disabled
fieldDocs.description: true if the user account was disabled

fieldDocs.name: roles

name: AppVersion
description: One recorded change to a row of a versioned type: who made it, when, and which fields it touched. A row's version column names the record describing the state it is in now, and prev chains that record to the one before it, so the fields changed between any two versions are the union of the masks in between. Written only by the merge, pruned after the version record lifetime -- which is why nothing has a foreign key onto it: a row outlives the records describing how it got here.

fieldDocs.name: created
fieldDocs.description: When the change was made. What the cleanup of expired version records goes by.

fieldDocs.name: entityId
fieldDocs.description: Id of the row that changed

fieldDocs.name: entityType
fieldDocs.description: GraphQL name of the type whose row changed

fieldDocs.name: fieldLayout
fieldDocs.description: Hash of the field-name list the mask was written against. A record whose layout does not match the schema in front of us has its mask read as unknown, so a deployment that reorders fields makes a mask conservative rather than wrong.

fieldDocs.name: fieldMask
fieldDocs.description: Bit per field of the type, set for the fields this change touched. The bit index is the position of the field in the type's alphabetically sorted field list, and fieldLayout is what makes reading that back safe.

fieldDocs.name: id
fieldDocs.description: Version id, and what the version column of the changed row holds

fieldDocs.name: ownerId
fieldDocs.description: The user who made the change. What lets a subscriber filter out its own writes.

fieldDocs.name: prev
fieldDocs.description: The version this change was made against, or null for the first recorded change of the row. Best-effort: the record it names may have been pruned, which reads as "assume every field changed" rather than as an error.

name: CNode
description: Abstract base class for all types in the FilterDSL condition hierarchy.

fieldDocs.name: type
fieldDocs.description:
The discriminator the FilterDSL JSON carries, derived from the class name. It is read-only in both
directions of the word: there is no field behind it, and a parser must not try to set it. It is
still generated, because it is what tells a reader which node it is looking at -- see
ConditionParser, which selects the subclass by it.

fieldDocs.name: header
fieldDocs.description: Header name to send the CSRF token as

fieldDocs.name: param
fieldDocs.description: HTTP Parameter name to send the CSRF token as

name: ConditionParser
description:
Specialized JSONParser setup to parse a FilterDSL node hierarchy into
the correct types.

name: FunctionNode
description: Implemented by operation and condition nodes which are all just defined by their name and their operands.

name: Injection

fieldDocs.name: type
fieldDocs.description: The GraphQL type of the injection

name: ModuleFunctionReferences

fieldDocs.name: requires
fieldDocs.description: Map of variable names mapping to

name: QLiveBoostrap
description:
Encapsulates the data for a /api/bootstrap call or to be embedded in the HTML document.

 * QLive config - QLiveConfig wrapped in a JSONHolder
 * injected data - Prepared data for the starting view based on static analysis of TypeScript sources.

fieldDocs.name: config
fieldDocs.description:
QLive system config.

We keep it wrapped in a JSONHolder to generate the JSON only once.

description: Contains the system configuration of a QLive system.

name: TrackUsageData

name: ValueNode
